lesson-intro.text: A bonsai is a real tree kept tiny in a tray, trimmed for years until it looks old and windswept. Pot first, then the twisty trunk, then the green. Watch it take its time, then shape your own.

pot-rim.text: The pot is low and wide. Begin with its rim, a long thin box with round corners.

pot-body.text: Under the rim, two short lines lean in to a flat bottom. Then tuck two little square feet below.

trunk-left.text: The trunk wiggles like a letter S. From the rim, wind up the left and out along the low branch.

trunk-middle.text: From that branch's end, curve back in and climb to where the top will sit.

trunk-right.text: Come down the other side and swing out to the right branch. Then wind all the way back to the pot.

top-pad.text: Each layer of green has a flat bottom and three bumps on top. Sit the biggest on the trunk's tip.

left-pad.text: A smaller layer rests on the low left branch. Flat line first, then bump, bump, bump.

right-pad.text: One more on the right branch, a little higher than the left one.

side-green.text: The two side layers are dark green.

pot-color.text: The pot is blue, with a purple rim and feet.

lesson-outro.text: Years of patient trimming, and you did it in minutes. That little tree is yours.
